q: The data points lie roughly along a straight line, but not exactly. How do you draw a line on the graph, and why are the points not joined into a broken line?
a: The line is drawn so that it runs through the middle of the set of points: it is close to all the points, and there are roughly equal numbers of points on both sides of it. A broken line would join the random measurement errors too, but a straight line shows the general relationship in the phenomenon.

q: A line passes through the points $(2.0\,\text{s};\ 5.0\,\text{m})$ and $(6.0\,\text{s};\ 11.0\,\text{m})$. What is its equation $s = kt + b$?

The line of the measurements crosses the $y$-axis at $b = 80\,\text{g}$. What does $b$ tell you when $y$ is the combined mass of a measuring cylinder and a liquid and $x$ is the volume of the liquid? Is the mass directly proportional to the volume?
a: The constant term $b$ is the combined mass when there is $0\,\text{ml}$ of liquid, that is, the mass of the empty measuring cylinder, $80\,\text{g}$. The combined mass is not directly proportional to the volume, because the line does not pass through the origin: doubling the volume does not double the combined mass.
